new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work was listed, so the spot-check for silent works was done on the same work (extra fts queries above) and on the two earlier-pass sources in the same folder: Rivet 1947 'Les Indiens Malibú' ( and the JSA vol. 36 djvu text, lines 11100-11480) has no occurrence of accent/tonique/accentu/stress/syllab; it is a historical-geographical note with a wordlist of a dozen items from 16th-17th c. chroniclers and three Pacabuey words, and says nothing about stress. Loukotka 1968 pp. 244-245 is a group listing with sources only. Nothing missed.

sources.note: Nothing. Historical-geographical note on the Malibú/Mocana with a ~15-word vocabulary (pp. 143-144) compiled from 16th-17th c. chroniclers (Rodríguez de Medina 1579, Simón, Aguado, Castellanos); words are given in the chroniclers' Spanish spellings (e.g. tahána, man, entaha, ytaylaco, mayhan); no remark on pronunciation, accent or stress anywhere in the six pages.
